recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group wants a stronger or different consistency guarantee for included resources; no FHIR core source correction is needed for this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-47371 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and asked whether SubscriptionTopic filter timing requires subscription checks, includes, or revincludes to complete before server state changes; the resolution requested additional text clarifying independent, lightweight subscription processing.
initial_application: Commit f486594368f07012d3a5af1b6f6958cb98856588, linked from the Jira PR comment, added the non-blocking paragraph to source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-notes.xml under Filter Timing and Interactions.
additional_context: SubscriptionTopic is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-I minutes approved the Subscriptions block vote containing FHIR-47371 at 17-0-0, and the Zulip block-vote announcement plus issue-specific searches found no contradictory discussion. FHIR-39028 is relevant background for the pre-existing filter-timing section.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/subscriptiontopic/subscriptiontopic-notes.xml already says subscription processing is independent of the request changing system state, create/update/delete commits need not block for subscription evaluation, asynchronous processing is appropriate, included resources are not required to be strictly post-commit consistent, and subscription delays/failures should not affect the originating interaction.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published issue that established the surrounding SubscriptionTopic filter-timing guidance; FHIR-47371 clarifies that section rather than replacing it.
